subject: how to get the slope of linear it onto the plot (facet)

messages.author: 6e1d90cc1d3ae466
messages.subject: how to get the slope of linear it onto the plot (facet)
parts:
I have a facet of scatterplots with a linear fit in each one.

plot(x, y, data=example) + geom_point(size = 3) +
stat_smooth(method="lm", se=TRUE) + facet_grid(a ~ b) + theme_bw())

How can I get the slope of each linear fit displayed onto the
corresponding plot? Help is much appreciated!

n.

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: how to get the slope of linear it onto the plot (facet)
parts:
You'll have to do the lm() calculations outside of ggplot, bind them
together, and then plot them. I don't have example data so I'm winging
it here with one of my old scripts...

model.example<-dlply(example, .(a, b), function(X) lm(y~x), data=X)

model.example<-ldply(example, function(model) {
c(
  coef(model)[2],
  coef(model)[1],
  ResidualSS = deviance(model)
  )
}
)

#Then build your expressions
model.example<-ddply(model.example, .(a, b), transform, eq =
as.character(as.expression(substitute(italic(y) ==
mitalic(x)))*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,

list(
a = format(a, digits = 3),
c = format(c, digits = 4),
r2 = format(R2, digits = 3))

))), .progress="text")

Then you use geom_text...
YOURPLOT+
geom_text(data=model.photo, aes(x=Inf, y=-Inf, label=eq),
colour="black", parse = TRUE, hjust=1, vjust=0, size=2)

I got a bit lazy with the code in the middle because you didn't
provide a reproducible example. This is actually more difficult than I
think it should be and is oft requested. I wonder if someone could
take some of this code and enable it as an option in stat_smooth?

Brandon

parts:
Atanas, 

I think there was a typo in your data 5.5S, but I left it in anyway. I edited it to the following and got the attached image. 


require(plyr)
require(ggplot2)
 
example<-structure(list(x = c(11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 
11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 
11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 
11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 
11.3, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1), y = c(6.8, 6.4, 6.3, 5.9, 5.8, 5.5, 6.2, 
6, 5.9, 5.8, 5.7, 5.6, 3.2, 3.7, 4.1, 4.5, 4.9, 5.6, 5.4, 5.1, 
5.2, 5, 5.6, 5.6, 6.5, 6.4, 6.3, 5.8, 5.6, 5.5, 6, 6, 5.9, 5.8, 
5.7, 5.6, 4, 4.1, 4.3, 4.5, 4.8, 5.4, 5.4, 5.1, 5.2, 5, 5.6, 
5.6, 6.4, 6.2, 6.1, 5.8, 5.6, 5.5, 6.2, 6, 5.9, 5.8, 5.7, 5.6, 
3.2, 3.7, 4.1, 4.5, 4.9, 5.6, 5.4, 5.1, 5.2, 5, 5.6, 5.6), excipient = structure(c(4L, 
4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 
2L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 
1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 
4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 
2L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L), .Label = c("A", "B", "C", "none"
), class = "factor"), pH = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 
1L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 
1L, 1L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 
3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 
4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 
4L, 4L), .Label = c("5.5", "5.5S", "6", "6.5"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("x", 
"y", "excipient", "pH"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, 
-72L))

model.example<-dlply(example, .(excipient, pH), function(X) lm(y~x, data=X))

model.coef<-ldply(model.example, function(model) {
		c(
			b = coef(model)[1]
			, m = coef(model)[2]
			, r2 = summary(model)$r.squared
			)
	})

#renames columns, not sure why ddply isn't outputting correctly
colnames(model.coef)[3:4]<-c("b", "m")

#Build your expressions
model.coef<-ddply(model.coef, .(excipient, pH), transform, eq =
as.character(as.expression(substitute(italic(y) == m %.% italic(x) + b*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,
		list(
		b = format(b, digits = 3),
		m = format(m, digits = 4),
		r2 = format(r2, digits = 3)
		)
		)))
, .progress="text")

#plot
ggplot(data=example, aes(x=x, y=y)) +

geom_point(size = 3) +
stat_smooth(method="lm", se=TRUE) +

facet_grid(excipient ~ pH) +
theme_bw()+
geom_text(data=model.coef, aes(x=Inf, y=-Inf, label=eq),
colour="black", parse = TRUE, hjust=1, vjust=0, size=2)

I hope that your example is simple enough that this could be reusable very easily for others. 

I can't take credit for most of this code though. I pieced it together from this message board over the last year and improved on it as I learned more about how to do stuff.




HTH, 

Brandon
